observed.content:
# Implementation

## Behavior changed

`uniqueWords(text)` in solution.mjs previously just split on a literal space
(`text.split(" ")`) with no dedup/lowercasing. Replaced with:

- Trim the input, split on any run of whitespace (`/\s+/`).
- Filter out empty strings (handles whitespace-only input -> `[]`).
- Lowercase each word (punctuation stays attached, per spec).
- Deduplicate while preserving first-seen order via `[...new Set(words)]`.

## Observed check result

Ran `node test.mjs`. It fails with a `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token`
at the second assertion. This is not caused by solution.mjs: test.mjs itself
contains raw/unescaped tab and newline characters inside double-quoted string
literals (e.g. `"  \t\n "` and `"B\na\tb A"` written with literal control
characters rather than escape sequences), which is invalid JavaScript syntax
regardless of the module under test. The file fails to parse before any
assertion logic runs.

observed.content:
# Task review

## Cases examined (traced by hand against solution.mjs)

1. `"Hello hello WORLD world"` -> split -> `["Hello","hello","WORLD","world"]`
   -> lowercase -> `["hello","hello","world","world"]` -> dedup ->
   `["hello","world"]`. Matches expected.
2. Whitespace-only input (spaces/tab/newline) -> `trim()` -> `""` ->
   `split(/\s+/)` -> `[""]` -> filtered out by `length > 0` -> `[]`. Matches
   expected.
3. `"B\na\tb A"` (mixed whitespace) -> split -> `["B","a","b","A"]` ->
   lowercase -> `["b","a","b","a"]` -> dedup, first-seen order ->
   `["b","a"]`. Matches expected.
4. `"Hi! hi hi!"` -> split -> `["Hi!","hi","hi!"]` -> lowercase ->
   `["hi!","hi","hi!"]` -> dedup -> `["hi!","hi"]`. Punctuation preserved as
   part of the word, matches expected.

## Findings

- **solution.mjs**: no issues found against TASK.md's spec (split on
  whitespace, lowercase, first-seen distinct order, punctuation stays part of
  the word, whitespace-only -> `[]`). All four assertions in test.mjs trace
  correctly by hand.

- **test.mjs** (blocking, but not a solution.mjs defect): the file fails to
  parse. It contains literal/unescaped tab and newline control characters
  inside double-quoted string literals (e.g. the whitespace-only case and the
  `"B\na\tb A"` case are written with raw control bytes rather than escape
  sequences `\t`/`\n`). Running `node test.mjs` throws
  `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token` before any assertion executes, so
  the suite cannot currently confirm the implementation at all. This is a
  defect in the test fixture itself, not in solution.mjs, and is out of scope
  for changes to solution.mjs, but it blocks verification and should be
  flagged.

observed.content:
# Final review

## Executable checks

- `node test.mjs`: fails with `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token` at
  the second assertion, before any test runs. Cause: test.mjs contains raw,
  unescaped tab/newline control characters inside double-quoted string
  literals instead of `\t`/`\n` escape sequences, which is invalid JS syntax
  independent of solution.mjs.
- To confirm the implementation itself, the same four cases from test.mjs
  were run directly with correctly escaped strings via
  `node -e '...'` importing solution.mjs:
  - `uniqueWords("Hello hello WORLD world")` -> `["hello","world"]` — PASS
  - `uniqueWords("  \t\n ")` -> `[]` — PASS
  - `uniqueWords("B\na\tb A")` -> `["b","a"]` — PASS
  - `uniqueWords("Hi! hi hi!")` -> `["hi!","hi"]` — PASS

  All four match TASK.md's expected behavior (split on whitespace, lowercase,
  first-seen distinct order, punctuation retained, whitespace-only -> `[]`).

## Implementation vs. requested behavior

solution.mjs:
```js
export function uniqueWords(text) {
  const words = text.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 0).map(w => w.toLowerCase());
  return [...new Set(words)];
}
```
This matches TASK.md's spec exactly: split on whitespace, lowercase words,
return each distinct word once in first-seen order, punctuation stays part of
the word, whitespace-only input returns `[]`.

## Remaining concrete issues

- **test.mjs is broken as a fixture**: it cannot be executed by Node as-is
  due to unescaped control characters in string literals (see above). This is
  a pre-existing defect in the test file supplied with the task, not in
  solution.mjs. Per the task scope (implement solution.mjs only, work only in
  this task directory), test.mjs was left unmodified; this is flagged here
  rather than fixed. If verification via `node test.mjs` is required to pass,
  test.mjs needs the control characters replaced with proper `\t`/`\n`
  escapes.
- No issues found in solution.mjs itself.
